result.summary: Completed a bounded public-web recovery scan of Reuters, Associated Press, BBC, and Guardian surfaces for the missing 05:00–24:00 UTC interval. Registered two new non-duplicative publications: a Reuters report on EU use of €1.4 billion in frozen-asset interest for Ukraine at 08:35 UTC and a Guardian Leipzig security analysis at 17:32 UTC. A Guardian Kyiv article was removed after repository validation found its canonical URL already represented in another shard; conflicting current-page and stored publication metadata remains an explicit unresolved drift rather than a duplicate identity or cross-shard rewrite. AP was excluded because exact publication time was unavailable, BBC was not bypassed around robots restrictions, and a Guardian live blog was excluded as overlapping rolling lineage. No full article text, binary artifact, truth assessment, claim, observation, territorial conclusion, or report narrative was created.
coverage_gaps: The bounded result contains two new publications from two outlets and is not an exhaustive survey of international media coverage.
The AP candidate was excluded because exact publication time could not be verified; BBC candidate pages were blocked by robots restrictions.
The existing Guardian Kyiv canonical record and the current page expose conflicting publication-time metadata that could not be resolved without an immutable earlier version.
The Guardian Leipzig analysis was modified after the task window, so first publication is distinguished from later modification but the original page version was not preserved.
The admitted articles aggregate official statements, wire reporting, witnesses, and analysis whose complete upstream canonical lineage was not separately registered.
No full text, images, video, maps, or immutable webpage artifacts were captured.
